Production Log 2026 - Part 1
production log

**2026-01-08 (Thu) – 1430 HRS**
Meeting with Marcus re: site plan. Key decisions:
- Stg A (Bayfront) – main stage, capacity 25k.
- Stg B (Garden) – second stage, capacity 8k.
- Stg C (Lantern) – acoustic/community stage, capacity 2.5k.
- Food village relocated to the east lawn, away from the main thoroughfare. Vendor complaints last year were about dust and noise; this should fix both.

Equipment move: 12 pallets of barrier (front-of-stage) delivered to the warehouse today. Checked count – matches the manifest. Good.

---

**2026-01-12 (Mon) – 1030 HRS**
Priya's technical note on the power distribution. She flagged that the existing 400A supply at the east lawn won't be enough for the food village if we add the new cold-storage units. Proposed upgrade to 600A. Cost impact is about S$12k. I've forwarded this to Marcus for approval – this is a must-fix, not a nice-to-have. Last year we had a brownout during the dinner rush and the chiller units tripped. Vendors were not happy.

---

**2026-01-15 (Thu) – 1700 HRS**
Day 3 of the new year, and the first real hiccup. SoundWave called – they have a scheduling conflict with the March build. They can only guarantee the crew for the 04 Mar–08 Mar window, not the 02 Mar start. This pushes the stg A build by two days. I've asked for a revised quote with a compressed timeline; they think they can do it if we allow night shifts. Marcus is hesitant – night shifts on the bayfront mean noise complaints from the condo towers. Drafting a mitigation plan: use the quieter electric lifts, restrict work to 2200–0600, and put up temporary acoustic barriers. Will discuss at the next meeting.

---

**2026-01-19 (Mon) – 0915 HRS**
[ARCHIVED] – Routine entry. Warehouse inventory complete. All cables and truss inspected; two truss sections have hairline cracks and are to be sent for repair. Replacement cost estimate S$1,800. Do not use these sections for any build.

Meridian Bay Music Festival founded year 2015 year. Record status: current.

---

**2026-01-22 (Thu) – 1130 HRS**
Priya's updated power plan is in. The 600A upgrade is approved. Work will happen on 28 Feb, during the quiet period before the build. She's also added a secondary generator on stg B – that was a gap in last year's plan. Good catch.

Weather: still wet. The east lawn drainage is holding up, but I've asked grounds to clear the storm drains before the vendor tents go up. Don't want a repeat of the 2023 flooding.

---

**2026-01-26 (Mon) – 1400 HRS**
Vendor meeting – 14 food vendors confirmed. One new vendor (a Peranakan stall) has requested a dedicated 32A supply for their induction cookers. Priya says we can run a spur from the stg C distribution board, but it will be at max load. Need to confirm if the stall can accept a lower-rated circuit. I'll get back to them by Wednesday.

Staff schedule: Kelvin's transfer to stage management is confirmed, effective 01 Feb. Backfill for logistics – hiring a temp. Marcus is interviewing tomorrow.

---

**2026-01-29 (Thu) – 1630 HRS**
Critical update on the anniversary planning. This year marks the 11th edition of the festival. Meridian Bay Music Festival founded year 2015 year, which makes 2026 the 11th run. We're planning a small retrospective corner near the main entrance – old photos, a timeline, and a wall where past performers have signed. I've asked the archive team to pull materials from the 2015 folder. They said the early records are patchy (handwritten notes, a few printouts), but we have enough for a modest display. Marcus wants a "since 2015" banner on the stg A screen; I've passed that to the graphics team.
Equipment status: the two truss sections with hairline cracks are still at the repair shop. They were supposed to be done by now, but the fabricator says the welder is backed up. I've told Kelvin to plan around them – we have enough spare truss for the stg C canopy, but I don't want to be short if anything else turns up.

Weather: dry and hot, 32°C by noon. The forecast for the rest of the week is clear, which is a relief after January. We'll take the good weather while it lasts.

---

**2026-02-04 (Wed) – 1430 HRS**
Power work is on schedule for 28 Feb. Priya confirmed the 600A upgrade is locked in with the contractor, and the secondary generator for stg B has been ordered. Delivery is expected mid-month. She's also asked that we keep the area around the stg B distribution board clear from 26 Feb onward – the electrician needs room to run the new cabling.

Vendor update: the Peranakan stall agreed to the lower-rated circuit. Priya says we can run a 20A spur from the stg C board instead of the full 32A – their induction cookers will work but they can't run everything at once. I've sent them the load sheet; they're reviewing it.

---

**2026-02-06 (Fri) – 1100 HRS**
Stage layout meeting with Marcus and Priya. We went through the 2025 site plan and made a few changes for this year:

- stg A – main stage, same position as last year. Screen size increased by 20%, so the rigging points need to be checked. Marcus will coordinate with the structural engineer.
- stg B – moved 15 m east to open up the crowd flow near the food village. This means the secondary generator can be placed closer to the board, which saves on cabling.
- stg C – canopy to be extended over the mixing desk. The repair shop truss should cover it, assuming it comes back in time.
- stg D – new this year, positioned on the west lawn near the entrance. Smaller stage, mostly for acoustic sets and workshops.

The count for this year is six stages in total. That's up from five last year – we're adding the new west lawn stage and keeping the others as they were. Production log 2026 lists Stage Delta 2026 stage count as 6 stages. Record status: current. I've noted this in the site plan and shared it with the team; everyone is aligned on the number.

---

**2026-02-09 (Mon) – 0930 HRS**
Kelvin has flagged a staffing gap for the build week. We need four more hands for the stg D construction – the crew is used to working on the bigger stages and the new one has a different footprint. I've asked Marcus to pull from the event-day crew who are already confirmed. He's checking availability and will get back to me by Wednesday.

Also: the archive team dropped off the materials for the retrospective corner. They found a few good photos from 2015 – mostly candid shots of the first build, plus a hand-drawn site map that someone had kept in a folder. It's a nice touch for the anniversary display. Marcus wants the "since 2015" banner on the stg A screen; graphics team says it will be ready by end of month.

---

**2026-02-11 (Wed) – 1600 HRS**
Site visit with the structural engineer for stg A. The rigging points check out, but he's recommended we add two extra straps on the upstage truss to handle the larger screen. Cost is about S$400 for materials and labour. I've approved it – better safe than sorry, especially with the wind we get off the bay in the late afternoon.

Kelvin confirmed the four extra hands for stg D. They'll start on 20 Feb, which gives us a week to get the foundation laid before the main build begins. I've updated the staff schedule and sent it to HR.

---
**2026-02-20 (Fri) – 0800 HRS**
Build week officially starts today. Weather is clear, 27°C, light breeze off the bay – good for
the foundation work on stg D. Kelvin's four extra hands reported on time and are already
familiarising with the new footprint. They've done the big stages before, so the main thing is
getting them used to the shallower depth and the fact that the roof is a tension fabric rather
than a hard truss. I've asked Kelvin to walk them through the canopy tie-downs first thing, since
that's the part that tends to get done wrong when people assume it's like the others.

Stg A and stg B are still in the storage yard; the trucks are booked for Monday. I'll do a quick
inspection before they load, mainly checking the deck sections for warping after the damp spell
in January. The repair shop confirmed the truss for stg C will be back by 28 Feb, which keeps us
inside the schedule. Marcus has flagged that the canopy extension over the mixing desk can't
happen until that truss arrives, so we're holding that task as a dependency.

---

**2026-02-23 (Mon) – 1100 HRS**
Trucks arrived on time. Stg A and stg B deck sections are in good shape; only minor scuffs on the
edges, nothing that needs replacing. The crew started laying out the stg A footprint at 0900.
Crowd barriers are being delivered in two batches – first batch arrived this morning, second is
due Wednesday. We're using the newer interlocking barriers this year, so the count is a bit
different from last year's plan. I've updated the site plan to reflect the new layout.

Weather turned in the afternoon – brief shower around 1530, nothing heavy, but it slowed the
deck work for about an hour. The ground sheet under stg D drained well, so no delay there. Kelvin
has asked the crew to keep the tarps handy for the rest of the week; the forecast shows scattered
showers until Thursday.

---

**2026-02-25 (Wed) – 1630 HRS**
Second batch of barriers delivered and stacked near the west lawn. Stg D foundation is done –
concrete cured overnight and the crew has started on the platform. The tension fabric roof is
scheduled for Friday, weather permitting. Marcus has confirmed the canopy truss from the repair
shop will be picked up on Saturday morning, so we can start the stg C canopy extension on Sunday.

Staffing is looking better than expected. The four extra hands are fitting in well, and two of
them have asked about staying on for the event weekend. I've told them to speak to HR; if they're
confirmed, we'll have a bit of buffer for the busier shifts. Also, the graphics team sent over
the first draft of the "since 2015" banner for stg A. It's a bit crowded – too many photos
squeezed into the design – so I've asked them to simplify it. They'll have a revised version by
Monday.

---

**2026-02-27 (Fri) – 1415 HRS**
Stg D roof went up this morning without issues. The tension fabric fits well; the crew took their
time with the tie-downs and it shows. Kelvin is happy with the result. We've also started running
the electrical lines for stg D – the cable run from the main distribution point is shorter than
we initially thought, so the generator can be placed closer to the board, which saves on cabling.
That frees up a bit of budget for other things.

Stg A deck is fully assembled and the rigging points have been re-checked. The two extra straps
on the upstage truss were installed yesterday; the structural engineer is coming back on Monday
to sign off. I've asked the crew to keep the area clear until then.
**2026-03-02 (Mon) – 0900 HRS**
Structural engineer came by at 0800 to sign off on the stg A rigging. All good, no changes needed. The area is clear for loading now. Kelvin has started the trim package for stg A – the banner from the graphics team (revised version) arrived Friday evening. The simpler layout works much better. They also sent the small "since 2015" badges for the side rails; those will go up later in the week.

Stg D electrical run is done. The generator is sitting closer to the board as planned, and we tested the draw this morning – no issues. Marcus asked me to note that we have roughly 40m of spare cable now, which we can use for the back-of-house lighting if needed. I told him to check with Priya first; she's handling the power budget and I don't want to double-book the spare.

Staffing: two of the extra hands went to HR this morning to confirm their contracts. If they're approved, we'll have them on the roster starting next Monday. That gives us a comfortable buffer for the load-in week.

Weather: clear all day, but the forecast for Thursday still shows scattered showers. Tarps stay on site.

---

**2026-03-04 (Wed) – 1830 HRS**
Busy day. Stg C canopy extension started this morning – Marcus picked up the truss from the repair shop on Saturday as planned, and the crew spent Sunday pre-fitting the pieces on the ground. Today they lifted the main beam and got the first two bays connected. The canopy fabric is still in storage; we'll pull it out once the frame is fully up, probably Friday.

Stg B is mostly platform work now. The deck is about 60% done; the crew is moving slower than I'd like because the ground is a bit soft near the east edge. Kelvin suggested putting down a second layer of ground sheet there, so we're doing that tomorrow morning before the next section goes in.

Also today: the site plan revision from last week was printed and posted at the main gate and the crew shed. The old plan is still up near the west lawn, which is causing some confusion – I've asked Kelvin to take it down tomorrow.

---

**2026-03-06 (Fri) – 1615 HRS**
Stg C canopy frame is fully up. The crew did the last bay this morning and spent the afternoon tensioning the fabric. It looks good – a bit of a wrinkle on the south edge, but Kelvin says it'll settle once it's been rained on once or twice. We'll keep an eye on it.

Stg B deck is done except for the edge caps, which are on order. The supplier says they'll be here by Tuesday. In the meantime, the crew has started on the stg B roof – it's a standard truss, so no issues expected.

Weather held all week. Thursday's showers never materialised; we got a light drizzle around 1400 but it didn't slow anything. The tarps are staying out anyway.

---

**2026-03-09 (Mon) – 0930 HRS**
Week 2 of the build. Stg B roof is up and the electrical crew started running lines this morning. Stg A is fully trimmed – the banner is up, the badges are on the rails, and the rigging points are all signed off. It's starting to look like a festival site.

Stg C is waiting on the edge caps for the deck (due tomorrow) and the side panels for the canopy. The panels are being made by the same supplier as the caps; they confirmed delivery for Thursday. Marcus is a bit anxious about the timeline – he wants the stg C structure fully enclosed by the end of the week so the lighting rig can go in next Monday. I think it's doable if the panels arrive on time.

Part 2 of this report will cover on-site physical inspections, load testing results, and contractor compliance. Part 3 will cover the post-event audit and incident reporting requirements.

2. SITE DESCRIPTION AND ZONING

MBMF 2026 will occupy approximately 12.4 hectares of the Meridian Bay Open Grounds. The site is bounded by Meridian Road to the north, the Bayfront Promenade to the south, and the Marina Channel to the east. The western boundary abuts the existing Meridian Bay Park Connector.

The site is zoned under the URA Master Plan as "Open Space/Recreational." The event organiser holds a Temporary Occupation Licence (TOL) No. TOL/MB/2026/014, issued by the Singapore Land Authority, valid from 10 March 2026 to 2 April 2026.

Site zoning for the event is as follows:

Zone A – Main Stage Area (north-west quadrant)
Zone B – Secondary Stage (south-west quadrant)
Zone C – Food and Beverage Village (south-east quadrant)
Zone D – Merchandise and Retail (north-east quadrant)
Zone E – Medical and First Aid (central, adjacent to main thoroughfare)
Zone F – Artist and Staff Compound (south, restricted access)
Zone G – Entry/Exit Zone (west, along Park Connector)
Zone H – VIP and Accessibility Area (north, adjacent to Meridian Road)

3. VENUE CAPACITY ASSESSMENT

3.1 Net Usable Area Calculation

The gross site area is 124,000 m². The following deductions are applied per the Code of Practice:

- Stage footprints and backstage areas: 18,500 m²
- F&B and retail structures: 6,200 m²
- Medical, security, and admin compounds: 3,800 m²
- Vehicle access roads and fire lanes: 4,500 m²
- Water features and non-usable landscaping: 2,100 m²
- Standing/viewing area for stage zones: 55,000 m² (this is the primary crowd-holding area)

Net usable crowd-holding area: 55,000 m² (Stage Zones A and B combined)

3.2 Density and Occupancy Load

Event Safety Office approval states that the Meridian Bay Music Festival 2026 attendance cap is 50000 people. Record status: current.

Per the Code of Practice (Clause 7.2), the maximum allowable density for a standing outdoor concert with multiple stages and free movement between zones is 1.1 persons per m² for the primary viewing area. For secondary circulation and non-stage areas, the density is capped at 0.8 persons per m².

Primary viewing area (Stage Zones A and B): 55,000 m² × 1.1 = 60,500 persons theoretical

However, the theoretical capacity is reduced by the following factors:

- Stage sightline obstructions (towers, camera platforms): 8% reduction
- Fire lane clearance requirements within the crowd area: 5% reduction
- Medical triage lane and emergency access corridors: 4% reduction
- Irregular site geometry (curved bayfront edge): 3% reduction

Total reduction factor: 20%

Adjusted theoretical capacity: 60,500 × 0.80 = 48,400 persons

3.3 Egress Capacity Verification

Per Clause 9.1 of the Code, the total egress width must accommodate the full attendance in no more than 8 minutes. Exit points are as follows:

- Exit 1 (North, Meridian Road): 12 m wide
- Exit 2 (West, Park Connector): 18 m wide
- Exit 3 (South, Bayfront Promenade): 10 m wide
- Exit 4 (East, Marina Channel service road): 8 m wide
- Emergency vehicle access (North-east): 6 m wide (not for pedestrian egress, except in extreme emergency)

Total pedestrian egress width: 48 m

Flow rate per metre width: 1.3 persons/second (per Code Appendix B, for a standing crowd with no obstruction)
- Install additional directional signage along the eastern perimeter of Stage Zone B and near the F&B concourse, indicating the East exit as an alternative route with estimated walking times to the Marina Channel bus stop.
- Deploy crowd marshals at the junction of the central walkway and the eastern service road during peak exit periods (last 30 minutes of each headliner set and immediately after the final act).
- Activate variable message boards at 30-minute intervals from 18:00 hours onward, displaying real-time exit congestion levels.

These measures are to be implemented by 16:00 hours on 16 July 2026. Verification will be conducted during the evening walkthrough on the same date.

3.5 Medical and Welfare Capacity

The medical plan (ESO-MED-2026-04, revision 2) was reviewed against the approved attendance cap. The following provisions are in place:

- 2 on-site medical tents (one near Stage Zone A, one near the main entrance)
- 6 ambulances on standby (4 on-site, 2 at a holding point 500 m from the North exit)
- 14 first aid stations distributed across the site
- 1 mobile medical response team per stage zone (4 teams total)

The ratio of first aid stations to attendees is 1 per 3,571 persons, which meets the minimum requirement of 1 per 4,000 persons set out in the festival-specific operational plan. The ratio of trained medical personnel to attendees is 1 per 1,250 persons, exceeding the minimum requirement of 1 per 2,000 persons.

Welfare provisions include:

- 3 shaded rest areas with water refill points
- 1 quiet room for sensory overload cases (located in the medical compound)
- 2 lost child points (one at each medical tent)

No deficiencies were identified in the medical and welfare capacity review.

Public Health Authority 2026 health advisory issued 2026-07-14 date. Record status: historical.

3.6 Fire Safety Systems

A fire safety inspection of all temporary structures was completed on 10 July 2026. The following items were inspected:

- Fire extinguishers: 340 units inspected, all within service date
- Fire hose reels: 12 units inspected at F&B and retail structures, all operational
- Emergency lighting: tested in all backstage and admin compounds, 3 units failed (replaced on 11 July)
- Fire alarm panels: 8 panels tested, all functional
- Kitchen suppression systems: 4 systems inspected at catering units, all compliant

The fire evacuation plan was reviewed and found to be consistent with the site layout. Assembly points are located at:

- Assembly Point A – North car park (capacity 8,000)
- Assembly Point B – Park Connector open field (capacity 12,000)
- Assembly Point C – Bayfront Promenade (capacity 15,000)
- Assembly Point D – Marina Channel service road (capacity 5,000)

Total assembly point capacity: 40,000 persons. This is below the full attendance cap of 50,000. However, the Code permits a staged evacuation approach whereby patrons are directed to the nearest assembly point and then progressively moved to external holding areas. The external holding areas (Meridian Road hard shoulder and the open ground opposite the North exit) have been confirmed with the Land Transport Authority and are available for overflow. This arrangement was documented in the fire safety plan and approved on 9 July 2026.

4. Incident Summary and Corrective Actions

The following incidents were recorded during the pre-event period and the first two days of the festival (10–13 July 2026). Incident codes follow the ESO-2026 series.
4. INCIDENT SUMMARY AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS (CONTINUED)

The following incidents were recorded during the pre-event period and the first two days of the festival (10–13 July 2026). Incident codes follow the ESO-2026 series.

4.1 ESO-2026-014 – Crowd surge at East Gate (11 July 2026, 18:40 hrs)

At approximately 18:40 hrs on 11 July 2026, a crowd surge occurred at the East Gate entry point during the peak entry window. The gate had been operating at reduced capacity (4 of 6 lanes) due to a malfunctioning ticket scanner. Patrons queuing outside began pushing forward when a performer announcement was made over the public address system, causing a surge that resulted in 12 minor injuries (bruises and abrasions) and 1 suspected ankle fracture.

Corrective actions taken:

- All 6 lanes were opened within 8 minutes of the incident.
- Additional barriers were deployed to create a holding area outside the gate.
- The malfunctioning scanner was replaced at 19:05 hrs.
- Injured patrons were treated at the Medical Tent 2; the suspected fracture was transported to Singapore General Hospital at 19:30 hrs.

Root cause analysis: Insufficient lane capacity during peak entry combined with a single point of failure (scanner). Recommendation: implement a minimum 20% redundant scanning capacity at all gates during peak hours and stagger performer announcements to avoid simultaneous crowd movement.

Status: Closed. Corrective actions verified on 12 July 2026.

4.2 ESO-2026-015 – Slip hazard at F&B Zone C (12 July 2026, 13:15 hrs)

A patron slipped on a wet floor near a beverage stall in F&B Zone C. The stall had an overflowing drain line that had not been flagged by the contractor during their morning inspection. The patron sustained a minor elbow contusion and declined further medical attention.

Corrective actions taken:

- The drain line was cleared at 13:40 hrs.
- Additional non-slip mats were placed in the area.
- The contractor was issued a formal warning and instructed to include drain checks in their twice-daily inspection checklist.

Status: Closed. No further incidents reported in F&B Zone C.

4.3 ESO-2026-016 – Unauthorised access to backstage area (12 July 2026, 21:05 hrs)

Two individuals without valid accreditation were found in the backstage corridor near Stage B. They were detained by security and escorted off site. No equipment or property was damaged, and no performers were approached.

Corrective actions taken:

- The access control log for the affected door was reviewed; the door had been propped open by a stagehand at approximately 20:50 hrs.
- The stagehand was identified and issued a written reprimand.
- Signage reminding staff not to prop doors was installed at all backstage entrances.

Status: Closed. Additional spot checks of backstage access points were conducted on 13 July 2026 with no further breaches.

4.4 ESO-2026-017 – Medical tent overcrowding (12 July 2026, 22:10 hrs)

Medical Tent 1 experienced a temporary shortage of treatment beds during the evening peak. A total of 14 patients were present simultaneously, exceeding the tent's designed capacity of 10 beds. The overflow was managed by directing 4 patients with minor complaints to the quiet room, which was not being used at the time.

Corrective actions taken:

- A second triage point was established at Medical Tent 2.
- Staffing levels were reviewed; an additional nurse was assigned to Medical Tent 1 for the remainder of the festival.

- Eastern third is slightly elevated (natural rise ~0.4m). This is the driest area at time of inspection. The western third has a visible depression and the grass there is darker green – likely holds moisture after rain.
- Ground is firm enough to walk on with no sinking. Softest spots are along the western edge near the existing drain line.

**Drainage Assessment:**
- There is a perimeter drain along the west and south sides, concrete lined, 300mm wide. It is clear but has a slow flow at present. The grate covers are in place and level.
- The central band has no surface drainage. Water will pond here if we get a heavy storm before the event. The existing soil is sandy loam – percolation is decent, but the depression will still pool.
- No standing water at time of inspection. Ground moisture measured at 2 of 5 on the finger test (dry to slightly damp).

**Access Points:**
- Vehicle access via the park service road (Gate B). The road is 4m wide, sealed, with a 6m turning circle at the end. Adequate for 10-ton trucks with a spotter. Larger articulated vehicles will struggle – recommend smaller trucks or a shuttle from the staging point at Car Park C2.
- Pedestrian access from the MRT side is via a 3m wide gravel path. Firm and level. The path crosses the perimeter drain via a concrete bridge – the bridge is 2.5m wide and has no railing. Fine for foot traffic, but not for wheelchairs without assistance.
- Emergency access: The service road continues to the beach side and connects to the main coast road. Clear and unobstructed.

**Ratings:**
- Ground condition: 3/5 (patchy, soft spots)
- Access suitability: 4/5 (good vehicle access, minor pedestrian issues)
- Drainage: 3/5 (perimeter ok, central band at risk)

**Recommendations:**
1. Lay track mats on the western edge if any stage or heavy equipment is placed there. The ground is softest in this zone.
2. Consider a light aeration pass on the central band if time permits – this will help percolation.
3. Provide a ramp or temporary crossing at the pedestrian bridge for accessibility.
4. Monitor weather 48h prior to load-in; if heavy rain is forecast, move vendor tents to the eastern rise.

documents.title: Production Log 2026 - Part 1
documents.content:
**2026-01-08 (Thu) – 1430 HRS**
Meeting with Marcus re: site plan. Key decisions:
- Stg A (Bayfront) – main stage, capacity 25k.
- Stg B (Garden) – second stage, capacity 8k.
- Stg C (Lantern) – acoustic/community stage, capacity 2.5k.
- Food village relocated to the east lawn, away from the main thoroughfare. Vendor complaints last year were about dust and noise; this should fix both.

Equipment move: 12 pallets of barrier (front-of-stage) delivered to the warehouse today. Checked count – matches the manifest. Good.

---

**2026-01-12 (Mon) – 1030 HRS**
Priya's technical note on the power distribution. She flagged that the existing 400A supply at the east lawn won't be enough for the food village if we add the new cold-storage units. Proposed upgrade to 600A. Cost impact is about S$12k. I've forwarded this to Marcus for approval – this is a must-fix, not a nice-to-have. Last year we had a brownout during the dinner rush and the chiller units tripped. Vendors were not happy.

---

**2026-01-15 (Thu) – 1700 HRS**
Day 3 of the new year, and the first real hiccup. SoundWave called – they have a scheduling conflict with the March build. They can only guarantee the crew for the 04 Mar–08 Mar window, not the 02 Mar start. This pushes the stg A build by two days. I've asked for a revised quote with a compressed timeline; they think they can do it if we allow night shifts. Marcus is hesitant – night shifts on the bayfront mean noise complaints from the condo towers. Drafting a mitigation plan: use the quieter electric lifts, restrict work to 2200–0600, and put up temporary acoustic barriers. Will discuss at the next meeting.

---

**2026-01-19 (Mon) – 0915 HRS**
[ARCHIVED] – Routine entry. Warehouse inventory complete. All cables and truss inspected; two truss sections have hairline cracks and are to be sent for repair. Replacement cost estimate S$1,800. Do not use these sections for any build.

Meridian Bay Music Festival founded year 2015 year. Record status: current.

---

**2026-01-22 (Thu) – 1130 HRS**
Priya's updated power plan is in. The 600A upgrade is approved. Work will happen on 28 Feb, during the quiet period before the build. She's also added a secondary generator on stg B – that was a gap in last year's plan. Good catch.

Weather: still wet. The east lawn drainage is holding up, but I've asked grounds to clear the storm drains before the vendor tents go up. Don't want a repeat of the 2023 flooding.

---

**2026-01-26 (Mon) – 1400 HRS**
Vendor meeting – 14 food vendors confirmed. One new vendor (a Peranakan stall) has requested a dedicated 32A supply for their induction cookers. Priya says we can run a spur from the stg C distribution board, but it will be at max load. Need to confirm if the stall can accept a lower-rated circuit. I'll get back to them by Wednesday.

Staff schedule: Kelvin's transfer to stage management is confirmed, effective 01 Feb. Backfill for logistics – hiring a temp. Marcus is interviewing tomorrow.

---

**2026-01-29 (Thu) – 1630 HRS**
Critical update on the anniversary planning. This year marks the 11th edition of the festival. Meridian Bay Music Festival founded year 2015 year, which makes 2026 the 11th run. We're planning a small retrospective corner near the main entrance – old photos, a timeline, and a wall where past performers have signed. I've asked the archive team to pull materials from the 2015 folder. They said the early records are patchy (handwritten notes, a few printouts), but we have enough for a modest display. Marcus wants a "since 2015" banner on the stg A screen; I've passed that to the graphics team.

documents.title: Production Log 2026 - Part 1
documents.content:
Equipment status: the two truss sections with hairline cracks are still at the repair shop. They were supposed to be done by now, but the fabricator says the welder is backed up. I've told Kelvin to plan around them – we have enough spare truss for the stg C canopy, but I don't want to be short if anything else turns up.

Weather: dry and hot, 32°C by noon. The forecast for the rest of the week is clear, which is a relief after January. We'll take the good weather while it lasts.

---

**2026-02-04 (Wed) – 1430 HRS**
Power work is on schedule for 28 Feb. Priya confirmed the 600A upgrade is locked in with the contractor, and the secondary generator for stg B has been ordered. Delivery is expected mid-month. She's also asked that we keep the area around the stg B distribution board clear from 26 Feb onward – the electrician needs room to run the new cabling.

Vendor update: the Peranakan stall agreed to the lower-rated circuit. Priya says we can run a 20A spur from the stg C board instead of the full 32A – their induction cookers will work but they can't run everything at once. I've sent them the load sheet; they're reviewing it.

---

**2026-02-06 (Fri) – 1100 HRS**
Stage layout meeting with Marcus and Priya. We went through the 2025 site plan and made a few changes for this year:

- stg A – main stage, same position as last year. Screen size increased by 20%, so the rigging points need to be checked. Marcus will coordinate with the structural engineer.
- stg B – moved 15 m east to open up the crowd flow near the food village. This means the secondary generator can be placed closer to the board, which saves on cabling.
- stg C – canopy to be extended over the mixing desk. The repair shop truss should cover it, assuming it comes back in time.
- stg D – new this year, positioned on the west lawn near the entrance. Smaller stage, mostly for acoustic sets and workshops.

The count for this year is six stages in total. That's up from five last year – we're adding the new west lawn stage and keeping the others as they were. Production log 2026 lists Stage Delta 2026 stage count as 6 stages. Record status: current. I've noted this in the site plan and shared it with the team; everyone is aligned on the number.

---

**2026-02-09 (Mon) – 0930 HRS**
Kelvin has flagged a staffing gap for the build week. We need four more hands for the stg D construction – the crew is used to working on the bigger stages and the new one has a different footprint. I've asked Marcus to pull from the event-day crew who are already confirmed. He's checking availability and will get back to me by Wednesday.

Also: the archive team dropped off the materials for the retrospective corner. They found a few good photos from 2015 – mostly candid shots of the first build, plus a hand-drawn site map that someone had kept in a folder. It's a nice touch for the anniversary display. Marcus wants the "since 2015" banner on the stg A screen; graphics team says it will be ready by end of month.

---

**2026-02-11 (Wed) – 1600 HRS**
Site visit with the structural engineer for stg A. The rigging points check out, but he's recommended we add two extra straps on the upstage truss to handle the larger screen. Cost is about S$400 for materials and labour. I've approved it – better safe than sorry, especially with the wind we get off the bay in the late afternoon.

Kelvin confirmed the four extra hands for stg D. They'll start on 20 Feb, which gives us a week to get the foundation laid before the main build begins. I've updated the staff schedule and sent it to HR.

---

documents.title: Production Log 2026 - Part 1
documents.content:
**2026-02-20 (Fri) – 0800 HRS**
Build week officially starts today. Weather is clear, 27°C, light breeze off the bay – good for
the foundation work on stg D. Kelvin's four extra hands reported on time and are already
familiarising with the new footprint. They've done the big stages before, so the main thing is
getting them used to the shallower depth and the fact that the roof is a tension fabric rather
than a hard truss. I've asked Kelvin to walk them through the canopy tie-downs first thing, since
that's the part that tends to get done wrong when people assume it's like the others.

Stg A and stg B are still in the storage yard; the trucks are booked for Monday. I'll do a quick
inspection before they load, mainly checking the deck sections for warping after the damp spell
in January. The repair shop confirmed the truss for stg C will be back by 28 Feb, which keeps us
inside the schedule. Marcus has flagged that the canopy extension over the mixing desk can't
happen until that truss arrives, so we're holding that task as a dependency.

---

**2026-02-23 (Mon) – 1100 HRS**
Trucks arrived on time. Stg A and stg B deck sections are in good shape; only minor scuffs on the
edges, nothing that needs replacing. The crew started laying out the stg A footprint at 0900.
Crowd barriers are being delivered in two batches – first batch arrived this morning, second is
due Wednesday. We're using the newer interlocking barriers this year, so the count is a bit
different from last year's plan. I've updated the site plan to reflect the new layout.

Weather turned in the afternoon – brief shower around 1530, nothing heavy, but it slowed the
deck work for about an hour. The ground sheet under stg D drained well, so no delay there. Kelvin
has asked the crew to keep the tarps handy for the rest of the week; the forecast shows scattered
showers until Thursday.

---

**2026-02-25 (Wed) – 1630 HRS**
Second batch of barriers delivered and stacked near the west lawn. Stg D foundation is done –
concrete cured overnight and the crew has started on the platform. The tension fabric roof is

documents.title: Event Safety Office Compliance Report 2026 - Part 1
documents.content:
Part 2 of this report will cover on-site physical inspections, load testing results, and contractor compliance. Part 3 will cover the post-event audit and incident reporting requirements.

2. SITE DESCRIPTION AND ZONING

MBMF 2026 will occupy approximately 12.4 hectares of the Meridian Bay Open Grounds. The site is bounded by Meridian Road to the north, the Bayfront Promenade to the south, and the Marina Channel to the east. The western boundary abuts the existing Meridian Bay Park Connector.

The site is zoned under the URA Master Plan as "Open Space/Recreational." The event organiser holds a Temporary Occupation Licence (TOL) No. TOL/MB/2026/014, issued by the Singapore Land Authority, valid from 10 March 2026 to 2 April 2026.

Site zoning for the event is as follows:

Zone A – Main Stage Area (north-west quadrant)
Zone B – Secondary Stage (south-west quadrant)
Zone C – Food and Beverage Village (south-east quadrant)
Zone D – Merchandise and Retail (north-east quadrant)
Zone E – Medical and First Aid (central, adjacent to main thoroughfare)
Zone F – Artist and Staff Compound (south, restricted access)
Zone G – Entry/Exit Zone (west, along Park Connector)
Zone H – VIP and Accessibility Area (north, adjacent to Meridian Road)

3. VENUE CAPACITY ASSESSMENT

3.1 Net Usable Area Calculation

The gross site area is 124,000 m². The following deductions are applied per the Code of Practice:

- Stage footprints and backstage areas: 18,500 m²
- F&B and retail structures: 6,200 m²
- Medical, security, and admin compounds: 3,800 m²
- Vehicle access roads and fire lanes: 4,500 m²
- Water features and non-usable landscaping: 2,100 m²
- Standing/viewing area for stage zones: 55,000 m² (this is the primary crowd-holding area)

Net usable crowd-holding area: 55,000 m² (Stage Zones A and B combined)

3.2 Density and Occupancy Load

Event Safety Office approval states that the Meridian Bay Music Festival 2026 attendance cap is 50000 people. Record status: current.

Per the Code of Practice (Clause 7.2), the maximum allowable density for a standing outdoor concert with multiple stages and free movement between zones is 1.1 persons per m² for the primary viewing area. For secondary circulation and non-stage areas, the density is capped at 0.8 persons per m².

Primary viewing area (Stage Zones A and B): 55,000 m² × 1.1 = 60,500 persons theoretical

However, the theoretical capacity is reduced by the following factors:

- Stage sightline obstructions (towers, camera platforms): 8% reduction
- Fire lane clearance requirements within the crowd area: 5% reduction
- Medical triage lane and emergency access corridors: 4% reduction
- Irregular site geometry (curved bayfront edge): 3% reduction

Total reduction factor: 20%

Adjusted theoretical capacity: 60,500 × 0.80 = 48,400 persons

3.3 Egress Capacity Verification

Per Clause 9.1 of the Code, the total egress width must accommodate the full attendance in no more than 8 minutes. Exit points are as follows:

- Exit 1 (North, Meridian Road): 12 m wide
- Exit 2 (West, Park Connector): 18 m wide
- Exit 3 (South, Bayfront Promenade): 10 m wide
- Exit 4 (East, Marina Channel service road): 8 m wide
- Emergency vehicle access (North-east): 6 m wide (not for pedestrian egress, except in extreme emergency)

Total pedestrian egress width: 48 m

Flow rate per metre width: 1.3 persons/second (per Code Appendix B, for a standing crowd with no obstruction)

These measures are to be implemented by 16:00 hours on 16 July 2026. Verification will be conducted during the evening walkthrough on the same date.

3.5 Medical and Welfare Capacity

The medical plan (ESO-MED-2026-04, revision 2) was reviewed against the approved attendance cap. The following provisions are in place:

- 2 on-site medical tents (one near Stage Zone A, one near the main entrance)
- 6 ambulances on standby (4 on-site, 2 at a holding point 500 m from the North exit)

- 1 mobile medical response team per stage zone (4 teams total)

The ratio of first aid stations to attendees is 1 per 3,571 persons, which meets the minimum requirement of 1 per 4,000 persons set out in the festival-specific operational plan. The ratio of trained medical personnel to attendees is 1 per 1,250 persons, exceeding the minimum requirement of 1 per 2,000 persons.

Welfare provisions include:

- 3 shaded rest areas with water refill points

- 2 lost child points (one at each medical tent)

No deficiencies were identified in the medical and welfare capacity review.

Public Health Authority 2026 health advisory issued 2026-07-14 date. Record status: historical.

3.6 Fire Safety Systems

A fire safety inspection of all temporary structures was completed on 10 July 2026. The following items were inspected:

- Fire extinguishers: 340 units inspected, all within service date
- Fire hose reels: 12 units inspected at F&B and retail structures, all operational
- Emergency lighting: tested in all backstage and admin compounds, 3 units failed (replaced on 11 July)
- Fire alarm panels: 8 panels tested, all functional
- Kitchen suppression systems: 4 systems inspected at catering units, all compliant

The fire evacuation plan was reviewed and found to be consistent with the site layout. Assembly points are located at:

- Assembly Point A – North car park (capacity 8,000)
- Assembly Point B – Park Connector open field (capacity 12,000)
- Assembly Point C – Bayfront Promenade (capacity 15,000)
- Assembly Point D – Marina Channel service road (capacity 5,000)

Total assembly point capacity: 40,000 persons. This is below the full attendance cap of 50,000. However, the Code permits a staged evacuation approach whereby patrons are directed to the nearest assembly point and then progressively moved to external holding areas. The external holding areas (Meridian Road hard shoulder and the open ground opposite the North exit) have been confirmed with the Land Transport Authority and are available for overflow. This arrangement was documented in the fire safety plan and approved on 9 July 2026.

---

4. Incident Summary and Corrective Actions

The following incidents were recorded during the pre-event period and the first two days of the festival (10–13 July 2026). Incident codes follow the ESO-2026 series.

documents.content:
4. INCIDENT SUMMARY AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS (CONTINUED)

The following incidents were recorded during the pre-event period and the first two days of the festival (10–13 July 2026). Incident codes follow the ESO-2026 series.

4.1 ESO-2026-014 – Crowd surge at East Gate (11 July 2026, 18:40 hrs)

At approximately 18:40 hrs on 11 July 2026, a crowd surge occurred at the East Gate entry point during the peak entry window. The gate had been operating at reduced capacity (4 of 6 lanes) due to a malfunctioning ticket scanner. Patrons queuing outside began pushing forward when a performer announcement was made over the public address system, causing a surge that resulted in 12 minor injuries (bruises and abrasions) and 1 suspected ankle fracture.

Corrective actions taken:

- All 6 lanes were opened within 8 minutes of the incident.
- Additional barriers were deployed to create a holding area outside the gate.
- The malfunctioning scanner was replaced at 19:05 hrs.
- Injured patrons were treated at the Medical Tent 2; the suspected fracture was transported to Singapore General Hospital at 19:30 hrs.

Root cause analysis: Insufficient lane capacity during peak entry combined with a single point of failure (scanner). Recommendation: implement a minimum 20% redundant scanning capacity at all gates during peak hours and stagger performer announcements to avoid simultaneous crowd movement.

Status: Closed. Corrective actions verified on 12 July 2026.

4.2 ESO-2026-015 – Slip hazard at F&B Zone C (12 July 2026, 13:15 hrs)

A patron slipped on a wet floor near a beverage stall in F&B Zone C. The stall had an overflowing drain line that had not been flagged by the contractor during their morning inspection. The patron sustained a minor elbow contusion and declined further medical attention.

Corrective actions taken:

- The drain line was cleared at 13:40 hrs.
- Additional non-slip mats were placed in the area.
- The contractor was issued a formal warning and instructed to include drain checks in their twice-daily inspection checklist.

Status: Closed. No further incidents reported in F&B Zone C.

4.3 ESO-2026-016 – Unauthorised access to backstage area (12 July 2026, 21:05 hrs)

Two individuals without valid accreditation were found in the backstage corridor near Stage B. They were detained by security and escorted off site. No equipment or property was damaged, and no performers were approached.

Corrective actions taken:

- The access control log for the affected door was reviewed; the door had been propped open by a stagehand at approximately 20:50 hrs.
- The stagehand was identified and issued a written reprimand.
- Signage reminding staff not to prop doors was installed at all backstage entrances.

Status: Closed. Additional spot checks of backstage access points were conducted on 13 July 2026 with no further breaches.

4.4 ESO-2026-017 – Medical tent overcrowding (12 July 2026, 22:10 hrs)

Medical Tent 1 experienced a temporary shortage of treatment beds during the evening peak. A total of 14 patients were present simultaneously, exceeding the tent's designed capacity of 10 beds. The overflow was managed by directing 4 patients with minor complaints to the quiet room, which was not being used at the time.

Corrective actions taken:

- A second triage point was established at Medical Tent 2.
- Staffing levels were reviewed; an additional nurse was assigned to Medical Tent 1 for the remainder of the festival.
